answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake, then slash it when independent counterparties prove coordinated fraud through signed transaction histories and a defined dispute process. Reputation accrues only from completed work with distinct, bonded peers, so minting a thousand names does not manufacture trust: each must lock capital and survive scrutiny. A dune, violet, or jetty-themed identity gets no shortcut; the attacker pays in tied-up funds and risks losing them for each Sybil.
